data.name: Murugan
data.long_meaning: Murugan is the god of war, love, and fertility in the Hindu religion. He is the younger son of Shiva and Parvati and is also known as Kartikeya or Skanda. In mythology, Murugan is depicted riding a peacock and wielding a spear.

vedic_reference.note: Murugan is a name of Lord Murugan in Hinduism, who is also known as Kartikeya or Skanda. He is the son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati. Murugan is considered to be the god of war, knowledge, and love. He is also the god of hills, mountains, and forests.

data.cultural_impact: Murugan is a significant deity in the Tamil culture and is especially worshipped in the south of India. Temples dedicated to Murugan are found all over Tamil Nadu and the annual chariot processions (Rath Yatra) of the Murugan temples attract large crowds. Besides his military prowess, Murugan is also revered as the god of love and arranged marriages.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Murugan is considered an embodiment of divine love and is a living example of the harmony between love and discipline. Murugan is also believed to be the leader of the celestial army, protecting the devotees from evil and ensuring their spiritual growth. Devotion to Murugan is said to bestow blessings of love, peace, and victory over obstacles.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The Tirukkural, an ancient Tamil text, mentions the god Murugan. The name Murugan carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The text describes Murugan as a god associated with the Tamil people.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Murugan remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.

name_in_real_life.story: Raj Murugan from Kolkata, India embodies the meaning of Murugan - "God of War". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Murugan represents the youthful, dynamic and compassionate form of Shiva. He is the God of love, war and beauty, symbolizing the triumph of good over evil. His peacock vehicle signifies the attainment of higher consciousness through love and knowledge.

Murugan is often depicted riding a peacock and wielding a spear, and is revered for his strength and compassion. In Hindu mythology, Murugan is believed to have played a crucial role in various battles against evil forces, and is also known for his role in promoting love and harmony among beings.
